rs_2024.flood_ems_method: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping activation EMSR720 (event GLIDE FL-2024-000063-BRA, activated 2024-05-03) mapped the May 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods with semi-automatic SAR delineation (DEL products: COSMO-SkyMed, RADARSAT-2, PAZ) and photo-interpreted optical grading (GRA: Pleiades Neo, GeoEye-1, WorldView-3) on five small Taquari-valley AOIs — Guapore, Encantado, Roca Sales, Das Antas Dam, Santa Tereza. All '5-Flood' polygons (observedEventA 'Flooded area' and 'Flood trace', plus DEL_MONIT 'Maximum flood extent') were unioned per AOI+image date, minus the BLP hydrographyA permanent/reference-water layer, rasterized centre-in onto the ~90 m TPI_flood grid (area-weighted variant at >=50% coverage reported alongside), and scored ONLY inside the EMS AOI extents. IMPORTANT COVERAGE LIMIT: the EMS AOIs cover ~51.6-51.9 W, 29.0-29.3 S — Porto Alegre, Guaiba, Canoas, Eldorado do Sul and Sao Leopoldo were never mapped, so every score is Taquari-valley-only evidence, not AOI-wide. For each EMS image date E, IoU/F1/precision/recall compare EMS flood cells with TPI_flood Alto+ (>0.4) and Critico (>0.6) in (a) the observed band dated E (rain days E-3..E-1) and (b) the GFS 00Z run issued 24 h before E restricted to frames depicting dates <= E. 'Flagged before onset' measures the % of the EMS flood footprint already Alto+/Critico in the observed band dated 2024-04-29 and in the GFS runs issued 2024-04-26/27/28 (onset 2024-04-29 03:00Z; tools/warned_before.py evaluate/by_lead). Caveats: EMS polygons are imagery-mapped extent at a moment — they miss flooding under cloud/vegetation, GRA 'Flood trace' marks earlier water no longer present, and the EMS image date E pairs loosely with our frame convention (observed band E = rain E-3..E-1, GFS frames depicting E = rain E-2..E; docs/conventions-dates.md).

rs_2024.landslide_ems_method: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping activation EMSR720 photo-interpreted 497 landslide ('6-Mass Movement') polygons (~6.4 km²) on the five Taquari-valley AOIs (Guapore, Encantado, Roca Sales, Das Antas Dam, Santa Tereza) from post-event optical imagery acquired 2024-05-06..05-15 (Pleiades Neo, GeoEye-1) — the slides are UNDATED: imagery shows the scars, not the failure time, so every polygon is scored against the L37 event onset 2024-04-29 03:00Z. (A) Each member polygon takes every ~90 m TPI_slide cell it touches (all_touched rasterization clipped to the EMS AOI extents; centroid-cell variant alongside) and counts as warned when ANY touched cell is Alto+ (> 0.4) [Crítico > 0.6]; shares are reported as polygon counts and geodesic-area weighted. Sources: the observed series bands dated 2024-04-29..05-02 (curve) and the GFS 00Z runs issued 2024-04-28/27/26 (24/48/72 h before onset; max over d1..d3 _slide frames depicting dates <= the onset day — the warned_before by_lead convention). (B) Scar candidates = OPERA DIST-ALERT-HLS vegetation-loss polygons inside the same AOI extents (representative-point containment): hit rate = % of EMS polygons with a candidate within 100/500 m; precision = % of in-AOI candidates within 100/500 m of an EMS polygon (polygon-to-polygon, UTM 22S). Random baseline (science-review item D2): the same number of random placements per seed on steep terrain (T_slide > 0, i.e. NASADEM slope >= 15 deg — the scar product's own terrain gate, read from the case T_slide COG because the 1" steep15_1as.tif it used is a gitignored static asset) inside the AOI extents, each buffered to a circle whose area is drawn with replacement from the in-AOI candidate areas; 200 seeds; mean and 95 % interval (2.5/97.5 percentiles); lift = observed / baseline mean. Caveats: EMS mapped only five small AOIs — scores are Taquari-valley-only, not AOI-wide; slides are undated (post-event imagery); polygons are imagery-mapped extent at a moment and miss cloud/vegetation-hidden slides; any-cell-touched is more permissive than the published point-cell scoring of the 16,027-point inventory.

replay_v2.method: v2 = TPI re-scored with R computed on the 90 m TPI grid: P3 = 3-day IMERG sum over [D-3d, D) from the upstream imerg_daily.npz cube (0.1 deg; GEE NASA/GPM_L3/IMERG_V07 / GES DISC identical), percentiles p90/p95/p99 PER 0.1 deg cell (2001-2023, 3-day sums ending D+-30d step 3), both bilinear to the 90 m grid then rain_score; S = the case s_series bilinear to 90 m (unchanged); T = the existing t_slide/t_flood COGs; TPI = (R*S*T)^(1/3) = NaN on permanent water (JRC GSW occurrence>=50% at 30 m max-resampled to 90 m OR MCD12Q1 IGBP 17). Issued GFS frames: P3 = observed IMERG days < issue + GFS 0.25 deg days >= issue (L28b), percentiles at the depicted day E=I+k, S held at band I-1. All tools re-run with cog_suffix=_v2; scoring rules/anchors/thresholds identical to v1.
replay_v2.diagnosis: v1 R came from Earth Engine at ~1 km: IMERG 0.1 deg 3-day sums scored against a climatology asset exported at 10 km with NEAREST resampling (gee/tpi.py), baking ~10 km stair steps into r_series and the TPI; and no permanent-water mask, so the Guaiba lagoon / Jacui floodplain and large lakes carried finite TPI. v2 removes both artifacts; domain-mean R v2 vs v1 agrees within a few % on smooth areas (see r_check).

forecast_proof.question: Would the upstream-rain signal have warned Uruguaiana before the Oct 2026 Uruguay River flood?
forecast_proof.answer_short: Yes, 5 days before the river reached flood stage at Uruguaiana (Oct 5) and at Itaqui (ANA gauge 75900000 also above flood stage from Oct 5): satellite rain already observed over the upstream basin (IMERG Early) plus the NOAA GFS run of Sep 30 put the basin 3-day total above the season's 99th percentile. Second rise: 6 days before Oct 29 (>= p95, Oct 23). The GFS forecast alone did not flag either rise; local rain at Uruguaiana never reached its own 99th percentile.

signal.basin: Uruguay River upstream of the Uruguaiana gauge, HydroBASINS v1c lev07, 192,578 km2 (73-point 0.5 deg lattice)
signal.rain: basin-mean 3-day and 7-day totals ending D..D+6: observed IMERG Early (days < D) + NOAA GFS 00Z run of D (days >= D)
signal.climatology: NASA POWER IMERG Final daily 2001-2025, Sep-Nov; 3-day p95 62.5 / p99 100.3 mm; 7-day p95 119.5 / p99 152.1 mm

itaqui_flood_stage_2026-10-05.source: ANA telemetry 75900000 (Itaqui), daily median level >= 8.50 m from Oct 5

lead_time_days.gfs_forecast_only: no flag before either crossing (Sep 29 run: 50.7 mm 3-day vs p95 62.5; observed Sep 28-29: 93 mm)
lead_time_days.local_rain_at_uruguaiana: 72 h rain never >= local 3-day P99 (max 0.85x, Oct 6) -> a local-rain index would not have warned

false_alarms.p95_strict_median_basis: Sep 18 + Nov 1-6 (Nov 1-6 precede the Nov 12-13 red alert at 8.46-8.52 m)

where.method: river floodplain HAND <= 5 m (90 m HAND) inside the case area (Fronteira Oeste reach, lon -58.0..-55.3, lat -30.6..-28.2) vs the radar new-water candidate polygons at Uruguaiana (7 polygons, 1.85 km2, about 29 people)
where.reading: the signal points to the river floodplain, not to specific neighbourhoods (lift 1.9; the lift depends on the area chosen: 1.5 on the earlier 80 x 80 km box)
where.people_in_flagged_corridor_method: GPW v4.11 2020 unadjusted 30" x fraction of 90 m HAND cells <= 5 m

caveats: IMERG Final is not out for Sep-Nov 2026: observed rain is IMERG Early (Early ran 1.34x Final on RS 2024 Apr 27). Scaling Early by 1/1.34: Sep 30 basin 3-day 75.7 mm (< p99 100.3, >= p95 62.5) -> still 5 d before Oct 5 at p95; second rise first flag moves from Oct 23 to Oct 24 -> 5 d before Oct 29.
Flood-candidate polygons are candidates, never confirmed; 082D NISAR pairs are dominated by rice-paddy flooding and are not used here.

SGB publishes hours-ahead level forecasts (e.g. 9.91 m for 23:00 on Oct 13) and Defesa Civil RS issued alerts (cota de alerta Oct 28); no public alert dated before Oct 5 was found -> no claim of being earlier than official warnings.
'Would have given N days notice', never 'prevented'.

rs_uruguai_2026.tpi_replay_note: Local TPI-flood (IMERG Early rain vs the IMERG Final climatology, SMAP L4, terrain) over the Uruguay River reach of the Fronteira Oeste (Barra do Quaraí – São Borja) read Critical over the Uruguaiana region in the bands of Sep 30 – Oct 2 (rain Sep 28–30; 13,129 km² Critical on Sep 30, 6,121 km² of it on the HAND ≤ 5 m floodplain), 3–5 days before Uruguaiana reached flood stage on Oct 5, and again Oct 11 before the Oct 16 crest and Oct 24–25 before the Oct 29 rise. The NOAA GFS run of Sep 27 already showed Critical on the floodplain for Sep 29–30, the Sep 29 run for Sep 30, the Sep 30 run for Oct 1 (2,783 km²), the Oct 1 run for Oct 3–4. Caveat: IMERG Early runs wetter than Final; the river flood itself was driven by upstream-basin rain (see forecast_proof).

tpi_replay.definition: observed band D = IMERG Early rain over D-3..D-1 (Final not released) vs clim_imerg_0p1 (IMERG Final 2001-2023); GFS frame E = obs days < issue + GFS 00Z run days >= issue, 3 days ending E; S = SMAP L4 rootzone wetness (GEE SPL4SMGP/008, D-1 / issue-1); T = terrain_flood(HAND, slope); permanent water (JRC GSW >= 50 %) nodata; corridor = HAND <= 5 m cells; 0.01 deg grid; case area lon -58.0..-55.3, lat -30.6..-28.2 (Fronteira Oeste reach); GFS issues every 00Z Sep 25..Oct 31

tpi_replay_robustness.early_to_final_scaling: rain ÷1.34 (Early→Final, RS 2024 test): floodplain still Critical Sep 30 / Oct 1 (3,541 / 2,619 km²; unscaled 6,121 / 5,665), Oct 2 Critical 82 km², Sep 29 Critical 37 km²

specificity.note: lenient test: flood stage held Oct 5-21 and Oct 29-31; the false-alarm days are small (127-256 km²) vs 13,129 km² on Sep 30

tpi_replay_robustness.reading: right days for the big signals (Sep 30 – Oct 2, Oct 11, Oct 24–25 all precede a rise), with 3 small Critical days (Sep 20–22) not followed by flood stage; places only moderately (lift 1.34 over the floodplain)

nisar_agreement.definition: Per pass: hit_pct = share of that pass's NISAR-water cells (cells of the case TPI grid) the index without NISAR flagged High+ (> 0.4, alto_plus) / Critical (> 0.6, critico); area_pct = share of observed land cells flagged; lift = hit_pct / area_pct; ratio_vs_terrain (M1) = hit vs a same-area terrain-only map. observed = TPI_flood of the pass day; forecast.lead_Ld = NOAA GFS run issued L days before, valid on the pass day.
nisar_agreement.note: Scores the flood index WITHOUT NISAR (pass-day TPI and NOAA GFS runs issued 1-3 d before) against one NISAR pass's candidate water (HH < -18 dB, fixed-stretch frame, outside permanent water, observed cells only). Candidate water also lights flooded rice / irrigation: outside_floodplain_pct is the share of it with HAND > 5 m; rice ON the floodplain cannot be told apart. Single-pass threshold; towns/forest stay bright (double bounce) and are missed.
